_comment: Hand-worked known-answer cases for the T-S1-2 terrain extension (S1 lane contract rev 8, sections 5.2 and 6.1). Every expected value was worked BY HAND, independently of the implementation; the derivations are recorded per case below and expanded in SOURCES.md in this directory. Arrays are SYNTHETIC, built by the test file from the constructive parameters here (no captured bytes, no network). Region rule: z[row, col] = base + perCol * col + perRow * row over [cols[0], cols[1]); base null means nodata (NaN). Polygon boxes are [col0, row0, col1, row1] in cell units on the grid below (x = x0 + col * resM, y = y0 - row * resM); fractional col/row values exercise partial-pixel weights. Row 0 is the northernmost row.

cases.name: elev-bands-basic
cases.derivation: Polygon covers a grid-aligned 10x10 cell window (columns 2..11, rows 2..11; 100 cells). Column 11 is nodata (10 cells), so valid-elevation area is 90 cells and each remaining constant column contributes 10/90 = 1/9. Band membership by the frozen half-open rule: -100 is below-0 (band 0); 0 and 499.5 are [0, 500) (band 1, so 2/9); 500 is [500, 1000) (band 2, the inclusive lower edge); 1500 is [1500, 2000) (band 4); 2000 is [2000, 2500) (band 5); 2999.5 is [2500, 3000) (band 6); 3500 is [3500, 4000) (band 8); 4000 is 4000-plus (band 9, the top edge belongs to the open-ended band). Bands 3 and 7 have no cells. 1/9 = 0.1111... serializes to 0.111 and 2/9 = 0.2222... to 0.222 at 3 decimals. coveragePct = 100 * 90 / 100 = 90.0.

cases.name: elev-bands-partial-pixel
cases.derivation: Polygon spans x from column 4.5 to column 6.5 (half of column 4, all of column 5, half of column 6) over 10 full rows: total area 20 cell-equivalents, all valid. Exact partial-pixel weights give column 4 (499.5, band 1) 5/20 = 0.25, column 5 (500, band 2) 10/20 = 0.5, column 6 (1500, band 4) 5/20 = 0.25. No rectangular-window ratio produces these; the half-covered columns require exactextract partial-pixel weighting.

cases.name: aspect-excluded
cases.derivation: A uniform plane falling east (z = 700 - 30 * col, so p = -1, q = 0, downslope azimuth 90 = E, gradient magnitude 1) with one nodata cell at (row 8, col 8), well inside the 10x10-cell polygon (columns and rows 4..13, 100 cells). Valid-elevation area = 99 cells (the nodata cell drops out of the denominator). The 8 neighbors of the nodata cell lose their full Horn neighborhood: excluded = 8/99 = 0.080808... which serializes to 0.081. Every other valid cell has aspect exactly 90: E = 91/99 = 0.919191... which serializes to 0.919. flat = 0 (no zero-gradient cell). Serialized partition sum = 0.919 + 0.081 = 1.000. The weighted mean over cells that all point east is exactly 90.0 (E) under both candidate near-flat rules.

cases.name: flat-vs-south-split
cases.derivation: Left half constant 500 (exactly zero gradient: flat); right half z = 2000 - 30 * row falls south (q = +1, azimuth 180 = S, magnitude 1). Two equal grid-aligned boxes of 12 x 32 = 384 cells each, both at least two cells clear of the region junction and the array edge, so no kernel mixes regions and nothing is excluded: flat = 384/768 = 0.5, S = 0.5. The flat cells carry no aspect under either rule (they are excluded from the unweighted mean and carry exactly zero weight under gradient weighting), so both rules emit 180.0 (S).

cases.name: near-flat-control
cases.derivation: THE AGREEMENT CONTROL of the near-flat decision procedure. Both halves fall west (azimuth 270) but at different gradient magnitudes: left rises east at 15 m per cell (p = 0.5, magnitude 0.5), right at 30 m per cell (p = 1, magnitude 1). Equal 384-cell boxes. Rejected rule (full unit-vector weighting): mean of two identical unit vectors (-1, 0) is (-1, 0), azimuth 270.0. Adopted rule (gradient-magnitude weighting): mean gradient vector = (0.5 * (-0.5) + 0.5 * (-1.0), 0) = (-0.75, 0), the SAME direction, azimuth 270.0. The weights differ, the emitted value does not: 270.0 (W) under both rules.

cases.name: near-flat-disagreement
cases.derivation: THE DISAGREEMENT CASE of the near-flat decision procedure, hand-worked on both sides. NEAR-FLAT area: left plane falls east at 0.03125 m per cell (exactly representable in float32), so p = -0.03125/30 = -1/960, azimuth 90 (E), gradient magnitude 1/960 (a numerically tiny, meaningless direction signal). STEEP area: right plane falls south at 30 m per cell, azimuth 180 (S), magnitude 1. Boxes: near-flat 12 x 32 = 384 cells, steep 8 x 16 = 128 cells, a 3-to-1 area ratio, both clear of the junction and edges. REJECTED rule (full unit-vector weighting, the shipped methodVersion 2 behavior): mean unit vector = (3 * (1, 0) + 1 * (0, -1)) / 4 = (0.75, -0.25); azimuth = atan2(0.75, -0.25) = 180 - atan(3) in degrees = 180 - 71.56505117707799 = 108.43494882292201, serialized 108.4, cardinal E: the numerically meaningless near-flat direction dominates. ADOPTED rule (gradient-magnitude weighting): mean gradient vector = (3 * (1/960) * (1, 0) + 1 * (0, -1)) / 4 = (1/1280, -0.25); azimuth = 180 - atan((1/1280) / 0.25) in degrees = 180 - atan(0.003125) in degrees = 180 - 0.17904873 = 179.82095127, serialized 179.8, cardinal S: the terrain that actually has orientation carries the value. Normalized resultant under the adopted rule = |(1/1280, -0.25)| / ((3/960 + 1)/4) = 0.99689, far above the 1e-4 cancellation epsilon, so the value is emitted, not nulled.

cases.name: opposing-cancellation-extended
cases.derivation: The cancellation-epsilon contract survives on the extended path: equal 384-cell areas of azimuth 90 (left falls east, p = -0.5) and azimuth 270 (right falls west, p = +0.5) at equal gradient magnitude 0.5. The weighted mean gradient vector is (0.5 * 0.5 - 0.5 * 0.5, 0) = (0, 0); the normalized resultant is 0, below the 1e-4 epsilon, so aspectMeanDeg and aspectCardinal are null (never an arbitrary rounding-noise direction). The distribution still reports honestly: E = 0.5, W = 0.5.

cases.name: zero-valid-all-nodata-window
cases.derivation: The grid-aligned polygon covers rows and columns 2..5, a 4 x 4 area. The public reader pads its bounds by 60 m, exactly two 30 m cells on each side, so the read window is the full 8 x 8 raster. All 64 cells are nodata, so polygon-weighted valid-elevation area is zero. The availability gate emits exactly the explicit-unavailability record, with no elevation-band or aspect-distribution fraction keys. The shape is identical for extended false and true.

cases.name: zero-valid-polygon-finite-window
cases.derivation: The grid-aligned polygon covers the central rows and columns 2..5, exactly 16 cells, and every one is nodata. Its 60 m padded read window is the full 8 x 8 raster, where the other 64 - 16 = 48 cells are finite at 100 m. Exact polygon weighting assigns those exterior pixels zero area, so polygon-weighted valid-elevation area is zero. The availability gate therefore emits exactly the same explicit-unavailability record under extended false and true, with no stats or fraction keys. Raster nodata is stored as -9999, but neither that sentinel nor NaN survives serialization.
